angle: record quarter (rev +29%, PAT +78%) but management declined all guidance questions citing a securities notice
text: APAR just printed its best quarter ever — revenue +29% YoY, PAT +78%, all-time high margins. Then management declined every guidance question, citing a securities notice. Record numbers, zero forward visibility. That's why our Q1 read fell instead of rising.

angle: record print plus a raised FY27 margin target (23%) and data-centre revenue share goal lifted 30%→50%
text: Sterlite Tech Q1: revenue +87% YoY, EBITDA margin 20.8% vs 12.5% a year ago. More telling than the print — they raised the FY27 margin target to 23% and lifted the data-centre revenue share goal from 30% to 50%. Raising guidance into a strong quarter is rarer than it sounds.

angle: 175% YoY revenue growth but CCT concentration up 50%→65% and 77% international — faster top line, narrower base

angle: strong quarter but guidance deliberately not raised — restraint read as discipline
text: Thyrocare had a good quarter — revenue +24%, EBITDA margin up 226bps to 32.2%, PAT +34% — and still left guidance at mid-to-high teens, citing a high base and seasonality. Not raising into strength is information too. I read it as discipline, not timidity.

angle: opex growth guidance raised 15%→18-20% for 6-8 quarters with revenue guidance untouched
text: Nippon India AMC: PAT +27% YoY to ₹504cr, MF market share up 54bps to 9.04%. The change worth noting is on the cost line — opex growth now guided at 18-20% for the next 6-8 quarters, up from ~15%, for digital and brand. Revenue guidance untouched. Spending ahead of growth.

angle: revenue +42% YoY while lead utilisation fell to ~50% on Gulf scrap disruption — growth from copper/mix, not volume
text: Gravita's revenue rose 42% YoY last quarter — while lead capacity utilisation fell to about 50%. The Gulf conflict cut 15-20% of its scrap imports. So the growth came from copper and value-added mix, not volume. Two different stories in one print, and I'm watching the second.

angle: 20% volume beat vs 15% guide, but the tell was disclosure quality — specific share and utilisation-trigger numbers instead of adjectives
text: CCL Products did ~20% volume growth in Q1 against a 15% guide. What I noted more: management gave actual numbers — 6% share in South India, a stated 75% utilisation trigger for new capacity — instead of adjectives. Net debt down ₹110cr too. Guidance still held at 15%.

angle: EBITDA margin doubled 4%->8% on 28% revenue growth; UPI GTV 2.2x industry — operating leverage showing in numbers
text: Paytm's EBITDA margin doubled to 8% from 4% a year ago, on 28% revenue growth. Consumer UPI GTV grew 45%, about 2.2x the industry. Management now sees 15-20% margin in 2-3 years, possibly sooner. Operating leverage finally showing up in the numbers rather than the slides.

angle: EBITDA/kg guide raised mid-year on plant consolidation (5 units to 2) and pharma/food mix — structural not pricing
